title: Build and run with Maven or Gradle

richText: Maven and Gradle resolve dependencies, compile source, run tests, and package applications.
Maven uses pom.xml. Gradle uses build.gradle or build.gradle.kts. Choose the tool used by the project.
The Spring Boot build plugin adds tasks for running the application and producing an executable archive.
A starter supplies libraries. A build plugin performs build operations. They have different roles.
Keep Spring Boot dependency management so related library versions remain aligned.
The Maven wrapper uses the project’s selected Maven version. On Windows, use mvnw.cmd.
Maven phases run in order. package includes earlier phases such as compile and test.
verify includes checks after packaging. install also copies the artifact to the local Maven repository.
clean removes prior build output. It is a separate lifecycle operation.
spring-boot:run runs the application from compiled classes without requiring an executable JAR first.

example.title: Run and package a Maven application
description: Use a generated Spring Boot Maven project with the Boot plugin configured. Run commands from the project directory.
example.code:
./mvnw spring-boot:run

# After stopping the application:
./mvnw clean package
explanation: The first command starts the application for development.
The second builds the package and normally runs the project’s tests as part of Maven’s lifecycle.
The packaged artifact is written under target.

richText: The Gradle wrapper uses the project’s selected Gradle version. On Windows, use gradlew.bat.
With the Spring Boot Gradle plugin, bootRun starts the application and bootJar packages an executable JAR.
build runs the project’s build and verification tasks. bootJar alone does not imply that tests ran.

example.title: Run and package a Gradle application
description: Use a generated Spring Boot Gradle project. Run commands from its project directory.
example.code:
./gradlew bootRun

# After stopping the application:
./gradlew bootJar
explanation: bootRun starts the application from the project’s runtime classpath.
bootJar writes the executable archive under build/libs.

richText: For Maven, dependency:tree shows resolved dependencies and their relationships.
Use the resolved dependency list to investigate conflicting versions or a missing class. A successful download does not prove compatibility.
